issue.title: test_muse_invoke_survives_a_provider_the_watchdog_had_to_kill misses provider_teardown_stall.json after 300s under the loaded check lane, passes in isolation

task_type_fields.evidence:
Proposed by sase-1r5.1.4 (epic sase-1r5.1 phase "network-git-and-lease-adopt") as a
PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP and triaged by the sase-1r5.1 land agent.

- Failed once during `sase tool run check` in the 17-minute xdist scoped lane on
  2026-11-04 (phase sase-1r5.1.4 verification). The test hung for 300.18s and then failed
  because `provider_teardown_stall.json` was never written.
- An isolated serial rerun on clean HEAD passed. The phase's diff (credential retries in
  SDD network git and the operational-lease fetch) does not touch llm_provider,
  the completion watchdog, or Muse.
- Observed fail rate: 1 failure in 2 runs (1/1 under the loaded parallel lane, 0/1 run
  serially in isolation). The epic's later `just check` runs (sase-1r5.1.5 and the land
  agent's run f124f37f1c8aaf42489f17bfaf428899) passed.
- Looks load-sensitive: the stall marker is written by a provider the watchdog had to
  kill, so a slow provider start under xdist load may miss the marker before the kill.
  Related but distinct closed beads: sase-16i (the teardown watchdog reaped Muse providers
  in production) and sase-1k0 (a different loaded-lane watchdog test).
task_type_fields.repro_cmd: sase tool run check (xdist scoped lane under host load)

issue.creation_reason: A completion-watchdog test hung 300s under the loaded check lane and passed in isolation on clean HEAD, and no task tracks this node; epic sase-1r5.1's land agent is filing the follow-up its phase sase-1r5.1.4 proposed.
